text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened — service anomaly detected for model variants (v1.3.2) on hosted inference. Elevated error rates and token truncation observed. Auto-alert triggered.

Sara Chen: seeing client-side JSON parse errors & OOMs for long-context requests. Error spikes at ~10:12 UTC, p95 latency also crept up.

Mike R.: confirming logs — kv-cache misses and repeated recompile warnings. Looks like a regression after recent kernel selector tweak rolled yesterday.

Lia Gomez: paging oncall. Imran, you up?

oncall-rotation: Imran Patel is on-call for infra. Paging @Imran Patel now.

Imran Patel: on it. joining. Can we get a quick impact estimate? Which routes are hitting v1.3.2?

Sara Chen: most affected are /v1/generate and /v1/chat for large contexts (>4k). Early telemetry: ~8% of production requests routed to v1.3.2, error rate for that subset ~18%. Overall customer-visible errors ~1.4%.

Support Ops: flagged 3 customers with elevated error budgets: Acme, FinLedger, and BotPress. Support started outreach to Acme.

Imran Patel: immediate mitigation plan: 1) steer traffic off problematic variant to stable variant (v1.3.1-stable), 2) temporarily lower per-request token limits for affected routes, 3) disable v1.3.2 variant until rollback/patch. Any objections?

Mike R.: +1. Suggest do 1 & 2 quickly, disable after confirming traffic shift. Avoid a hard rollback until canary shows stable behavior.

Sara Chen: steps for steering — use routing policy to move 90% -> v1.3.1-stable, keep 10% for smoke checks. I'll run the routing change.

Sara Chen: running command:```bash
# steer 90% traffic from v1.3.2 -> v1.3.1-stable
redwoodctl routing update --model my-gen-model --variant v1.3.2 --steer-to v1.3.1-stable --percent 90 --reason "mitigate regression"
```

deploy-bot: Routing change applied (id: rt-20260315-289). Previous split: 100% v1.3.2 -> New split: 10% v1.3.2 / 90% v1.3.1-stable.

Imran Patel: good. Now applying temporary quota drop on streaming tokens for the affected routes to reduce amplifier risk. CLI:```bash
redwoodctl quotas update --route /v1/generate --max-tokens 2048 --note "temp mitigation"
redwoodctl quotas update --route /v1/chat --max-tokens 4096 --note "temp mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: Quota update queued and applied across regions.

Lia Gomez: Support Ops — please pause new trial onboarding for now and route payment-critical customers to the dedicated fallback if they show errors.

Support Ops: ack, pausing trial flows and opening priority cases for Acme/FinLedger/BotPress.

Imran Patel: once steering is confirmed stable for 15m we'll disable v1.3.2 to eliminate any risk of accidental routing. Command to disable variant (will set traffic to 0 and mark disabled):```bash
redwoodctl models disable-variant --model my-gen-model --variant v1.3.2 --reason "regression: high error rate" --notify-team "eng-runtime,eng-infra,product"
```

Sara Chen: monitoring metrics now — error rate for v1.3.2 dropping as expected due to steering. p99 latency on v1.3.1-stable unchanged. Keeping 10% for smoke.

Mike R.: also collecting logs for the kernel selector path and will start bisecting the commit range.

Imran Patel: after 20m of stable smoke we will disable. Imran taking lead — handing off to Mike for post-mortem root cause once incident is closed. Lia, please coordinate customer comms.

Lia Gomez: will draft a short blameless note and send to affected customers once we have timeline. Immediate note: "We temporarily routed traffic to a stable model variant to mitigate errors; no code changes required on your side."

Sara Chen: 20m smoke check complete. Traffic steering holding, errors on v1.3.2 bucket are negligible. Proceeding to disable.

Sara Chen: executing disable command now.```bash
# disable v1.3.2
redwoodctl models disable-variant --model my-gen-model --variant v1.3.2 --reason "temp disable after regression" --dry-run false
```

deploy-bot: Variant v1.3.2 marked disabled. Traffic now 0% for v1.3.2. Incident severity downgraded to S2.

Imran Patel: great. Customers should be on stable variant. Can we confirm no new errors from Acme/FinLedger/BotPress?

Support Ops: Acme reports flows back to normal. FinLedger acknowledging lower error rate; BotPress still reporting a couple of truncated responses, Support investigating specific prompts.

Mike R.: started bisecting kernel selector commits. Early suspect is commit c4b2f9 that changed attention block tiling. Will try revert in a non-prod canary.

Lia Gomez: sending a short customer advisory now. Will include timeline, mitigation steps, and next update ETA 3 hours.

Imran Patel: handoff note — I'm staying on for 1hr to validate telemetry and help with postmortem. Mike you own RCA and remediation. Sara continue monitoring and fold any remaining errors into the evals cohort.

Sara Chen: ack. Adding related eval prompts to the regression dashboard.

incident-bot: Incident update — mitigation applied: traffic steered to v1.3.1-stable; v1.3.2 disabled. Current status: recovering.

Support Ops: closing immediate paging loop; will re-open if new customer impact appears.

Imran Patel: final note for thread — action items: [Mike R. - root cause & revert plan], [Sara Chen - add prompts to evals and monitor], [Lia Gomez - customer comms], [Support Ops - follow ups with customers]. Marking this thread for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

Mike R.: noted. I'll post follow-up RFC for kernel tiling revert and a safer rollout checklist.

Lia Gomez: thanks team.

Sara Chen: :thumbsup:"
